questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

[Table: Age x (years): 1.25,2.25,3.5,4.4,5.85; mean weight y (kg): 10,13,14,17,19.] The regression line is y=ax+b.
(a) (i) Find a and b. (ii) Write down the correlation coefficient. [4]
(b) Estimate the mean weight of a child aged 1.95 years. [2]

2. [Maximum mark: 6]

The following diagram shows quadrilateral ABCD.

[Diagram not to scale: diagonal DB divides it into triangles ADB and DBC; AB=11 cm, BC=6 cm, ∠BAD=59°, ∠ADB=100°, ∠CBD=82°.]
(a) Find DB. [3]
(b) Find DC. [3]
questions.solution: (a) DB/sin59°=11/sin100°, so DB=9.57 cm. (b) In DBC, cosine rule gives DC²=DB²+6²−2(DB)(6)cos82°, hence DC=10.6 cm.

3. [Maximum mark: 5]

Let f(x)=sin(eˣ), 0≤x≤1.5. [Diagram: graph of f.]
(a) Find the x-intercept. [2]
(b) The region enclosed by f and the axes is rotated 360° about the x-axis. Find the volume. [3]
questions.summary: Find an intercept and volume numerically.

4. [Maximum mark: 7]

The first term of an infinite geometric sequence is 4. Its sum is 200.
(a) Find the common ratio. [2]
(b) Find the sum of the first 8 terms. [2]
(c) Find the least n for which Sₙ>163. [3]

5. [Maximum mark: 6]

Consider the expansion of (2x + k/x)⁹, where k > 0. The coefficient of the term in x³ is equal to the coefficient of the term in x⁵. Find k.
questions.solution: The x³ term occurs for r=3 and has coefficient C(9,3)2⁶k³=5376k³. The x⁵ term occurs for r=2 and has coefficient C(9,2)2⁷k²=4608k². Equating and using k>0 gives k=6/7.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 8]

A Ferris wheel of diameter 111 m rotates at constant speed. Its bottom is k metres above ground. A seat starts at the bottom. [Diagram not to scale.] One revolution takes 16 minutes.
(a) After 8 minutes the seat is 117 m high. Find k. [2]
After t minutes, h(t)=61.5+a cos(πt/8), 0≤t≤32.
(b) Find a. [3]
(c) Find when the seat is 30 m high for the third time. [3]
questions.solution: (a) At the top, k+111=117, so k=6. (b) h(0)=6 gives a=−55.5. (c) Solve 61.5−55.5cos(πt/8)=30; the third occurrence is t=18.5 min.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 7]

Let f(x)=(8x−5)/(cx+6), for x≠−6/c, c≠0.
(a) The line x=3 is a vertical asymptote. Find c. [2]
(b) Write down the horizontal asymptote. [2]
(c) The line y=k intersects the graph of |f(x)| at exactly one point. Find possible k. [3]
questions.solution: (a) 3c+6=0, so c=−2. (b) The horizontal asymptote is the ratio of leading coefficients, y=8/c=−4. (c) The graph of |f| has horizontal asymptote y=4 and one x-intercept, so a horizontal line meets it exactly once for k=0 or k=4.

8. [Maximum mark: 13]

P=(3,2,5), Q=(7,4,9), and PR⃗=6i−j+3k.
(a) (i) Find PQ⃗. (ii) Find |PQ⃗|. [4]
(b) Find the angle between PQ⃗ and PR⃗. [4]
(c) Find the area of triangle PQR. [2]
(d) Hence or otherwise find the shortest distance from R to the line through P and Q. [3]

9. [Maximum mark: 15]

A particle has velocity v(t)=7cost−5t, 0≤t≤7. [Diagram: graph of v against t.]
(a) Find initial velocity. [2]
(b) Find maximum speed. [3]
(c) Write down the number of times acceleration is 0. [3]
(d) Find acceleration when P changes direction. [4]
(e) Find total distance travelled. [3]
questions.solution: (a) 7 m s⁻¹. (b) Minimum v=−24.6571, so max speed=24.7. (c) a=v′=−7sint−5 has 3 zeros on [0,7]. (d) v=0 at t=0.863851; a=−9.25 m s⁻². (e) Integrate |v| over [0,7]: 63.9 m.

10. [Maximum mark: 17]

Apple mass M is normal with mean μ. [Table: M<93 has probability k; 93≤M≤119 has probability 0.98; M>119 has probability 0.01.]
(a) (i) Find k. (ii) Show μ=106. [4]
Apples below 95 g are small.
(b) Find P(M<95). [5]
Bags contain ten apples.
(c) Find the probability a bag has at most one small apple. [3]
A crate has 50 bags.
(d) (i) Find expected bags with at most one small apple. (ii) Find probability at least 48 such bags. [5]
